rules.quote: Alerts are defined as events that have security implications, and should be handled by the main processor, or escalated to other hardware modules to take action.
rules.condition: An alert event with security implications occurs
rules.statement: Alerts must be handled by the main processor or escalated to other hardware modules to take action.

rules.quote: Those peripherals should instantiate one module (prim_alert_sender) to convert the event associated with that alert into a signal to the alert handler module.
rules.condition: A peripheral defines one or more alert signals
rules.statement: Peripherals defining alerts should instantiate one prim_alert_sender module to convert the alert event into a signal to the alert handler.

rules.quote: Alerts are encoded differentially and signaled using a full handshake on the alert_tx_i/o.alert_p/n and alert_rx_i/o.ack_p/n wires.
rules.statement: Alerts are encoded differentially and signaled using a full handshake on the alert_p/n and ack_p/n wires.

rules.quote: The "native alert message" will be repeated on the output wires as long as the alert event is still true within the peripheral. The handshake pattern is repeated as long as the alert is true.
rules.condition: The alert event is still true within the peripheral
rules.statement: The alert sender must keep repeating the native alert message and handshake pattern on its output wires while the alert is true.

rules.quote: The sender will wait for 2 cycles between handshakes.
rules.statement: The sender waits 2 cycles between handshakes.

rules.quote: Note that the alert is immediately propagated to alert_o once the initial level change on alert_tx_i.alert_p/n has been received and synchronized to the local clock on the receiver side. This ensures that the first occurrence of an alert is always propagated - even if the handshake lines have been manipulated to emulate backpressure.
rules.condition: Initial level change on alert_tx_i.alert_p/n is received and synchronized, even if handshake lines are manipulated to emulate backpressure
rules.statement: The receiver must immediately propagate the first occurrence of an alert to alert_o.

rules.quote: The alert sender and receiver modules can either be used synchronously or asynchronously.
rules.statement: The alert sender and receiver modules may be used either synchronously or asynchronously.

rules.quote: The signaling protocol remains the same in both cases, but the additional synchronizer flops at the diff pair inputs may be omitted, which results in lower signaling latency.
rules.statement: The signaling protocol remains the same; the additional synchronizer flops at the diff pair inputs may be omitted, giving lower latency.

rules.quote: All differential pairs are monitored for signal integrity issues, and if an encoding failure is detected, the receiver module asserts a signal integrity alert via integ_fail_o. The alert_tx_i.alert_p/n pair is not correctly encoded on the receiver side. This can be directly flagged as an integrity failure on the receiver side.
rules.condition: The alert_tx_i.alert_p/n pair is not correctly encoded at the receiver
rules.statement: The receiver must assert integ_fail_o when alert_tx_i.alert_p/n is incorrectly encoded.

rules.quote: All differential pairs are monitored for signal integrity issues, and if an encoding failure is detected, the receiver module asserts a signal integrity alert via integ_fail_o. The alert_rx_i.ping_p/n or the alert_rx_i.ack_p/n pairs are not correctly encoded on the sender side. This is signaled to the receiver by setting the alert_tx_o.alert_p/n wires to the same value, and that value will be continuously toggled. This implicitly triggers a signal integrity alert on the receiver side.
rules.condition: The ping_p/n or ack_p/n pair is incorrectly encoded on the sender side
rules.statement: The sender must set alert_tx_o.alert_p/n to the same continuously toggling value, which triggers integ_fail_o on the receiver.

rules.quote: Note that if signal integrity failures occur during ping or alert handshaking, it is possible that the protocol state-machines lock up and the alert sender and receiver modules become unresponsive. However, the above mechanisms ensure that this will always trigger either a signal integrity alert or eventually a "pingfail" alert.
rules.condition: Signal integrity failures occur during ping or alert handshaking and the protocol state machines lock up
rules.statement: Such lock-up must always trigger either a signal integrity alert or eventually a pingfail alert.
